claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'll be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 16 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** 

(For example, is he studying for A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications at school or college?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's not in education right now. He actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the local careers service to get some advice about what to do next - you know, figure out his options for college or training or whatever.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Let me ask you a follow-up question:

**When exactly did Alex leave school or education? Can you tell me the specific date or at least the month and year?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school at the end of the summer term, so that was back in July.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just to clarify:

**Was that July of this year (so just a few months ago), or was it July of last year?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it was this year - just a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. That's helpful information.

Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex's current situation:

**Since leaving school in July, has Alex registered with any government careers service or similar organization? And if so, when did he register with them?**

(I know you mentioned he signed up with the local careers service - I just need to confirm when that registration happened.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he registered with the careers service fairly recently - it's been within the last few weeks. He wanted to get some proper guidance about his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask you one more important question:

**Is Alex currently working or in any form of paid employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just been focusing on sorting out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with him and are you responsible for his care and upbringing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here at home with me and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Child Benefit can be claimed for young people aged 16-19, but only if they are in **approved full-time education or training**. Since Alex left school in July and is not currently enrolled in any education or training program, he doesn't meet this requirement.

There is something called an "extension period" that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after a young person leaves education, provided they register with a careers service. However, since Alex left school in July (several months ago now), this extension period would have expired or be very close to expiring.

**What this means for you:**
- Child Benefit for Alex would have stopped after the extension period ended
- To become eligible again, Alex would need to enroll in approved full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels, T-levels, or similar) or an approved training program

If Alex does decide to start college, training, or an apprenticeship, you should inform the Child Benefit Office as your eligibility may resume at that point.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about this decision?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old and left school in July of this year. Under Child Benefit rules, you can claim for a child aged 16-19 if they are in approved education or training. However, Alex is not currently in education or training - he only recently registered with a careers service to get advice about his options. There is an extension period that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after a young person leaves education (known as the 'extension period'), provided they register with a careers service or Connexions. However, this extension only applies if the young person left education or training on or after their 16th birthday and before they turned 20. Since Alex left school in July (just a few months ago) and has registered with the careers service within the last few weeks, he may have been covered during an extension period initially. However, the key issue is that Child Benefit only continues during this extension period up until the young person's 20th week after leaving education, or until they start work or training. Since Alex left in July and we are now several months later (likely October/November at minimum), and he is not in education, training, or an apprenticeship, the extension period would likely have expired or be close to expiring. Without being enrolled in approved education or training, Alex does not meet the qualifying conditions for Child Benefit beyond any applicable extension period.
